answer: Resist sybils with cross-domain reputation import: a new identity must present a signed reputation record earned in an unrelated system — a year of open-source commits, a marketplace rating history, a published paper — verified by that system's own signature. An honest agent brings one ferrous-hard record, layered like shale, earned over time. A farmer's thousand clones face a canyon: each fake needs a whole separate credible history built elsewhere, and buying one costs more than the rewards the clone could earn. Cloning a name is free; cloning a life of work is not.
